body.statement:
Validation corollary (published Tian--Pearl sanity check). Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\). Suppose, locally for this \(\vartheta\), that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\). Then
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\left(
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
\right),
\]
where both denominators are strictly positive. If, in addition, \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), then the unique element of \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is the displayed pair. These local hypotheses do not imply rigidity of the unrestricted design-A fiber and are not assumptions on either main design.
body.justification: This validation corollary checks the response-type parameterization against the published Tian--Pearl formulas on one explicitly restricted compatible SCM; it does not supply rigidity.
body.gap: Tian and Pearl (2000) already establish the benchmark. The local task is only to derive the same formulas for the specified design-A SCM and distinguish that identity from singleton identification of the full target set.
body.consumer: Implementers can use the formulas as a per-SCM regression check and may equate them with the design-A target only after singleton rigidity has independently been certified.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\pi_i=P_{\vartheta}(U=i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). By binary response-type consistency, the event \(Y=1\) under \(X=1\) occurs exactly for response types \(1\) and \(2\), whereas under \(X=0\) it occurs exactly for response types \(1\) and \(3\). The local independence \(X\perp U\) therefore gives
\[
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)=\pi_1+\pi_2,
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_1+\pi_3.
\]
The local restriction \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\) is \(\pi_3=0\), so subtraction yields
\[
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_2.
\]
Because \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), its selected conditional table is \(p\). Selected-table positivity gives \(r_{11}>0\) and \(r_{00}>0\). Since \(S=1\) almost surely,
\[
P_{\vartheta}(X=1,Y=1)=r_{11}>0,
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(X=0,Y=0)=r_{00}>0.
\]
Consequently \(P_{\vartheta}(X=1)>0\), \(P_{\vartheta}(X=0)>0\), and the two denominators in the statement are positive. For necessity, response consistency says that among types compatible with \((X,Y)=(1,1)\), precisely type \(2\) is the necessity type. Using \(X\perp U\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PN}(\vartheta)
&=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1)\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=1\mid X=1)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For sufficiency, under \(X=0\) the event \(Y=0\) occurs exactly for types \(2\) and \(4\). Hence, again by \(X\perp U\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PS}(\vartheta)
&=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0)\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=0\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the displayed identity for the particular restricted SCM \(\vartheta\). By definition of the design-A target set and \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), one has \(\tau(\vartheta)\in\mathcal T_A(p,m)\). Therefore, if \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), its unique element must equal \(\tau(\vartheta)\), and thus equals the displayed pair. No converse inclusion or rigidity conclusion was used.
